content:
<Rep. Jamie Raskin>: This is an absurd bill that reveals just how much my colleagues are opposed to immigration in all its forms, including legal immigration. This bill purports to authorize a review of all immigration benefits approved during the last five years for individuals from countries President Donald Trump has decided to place on his latest discriminatory travel ban--that includes the case of every green card that was issued, of every person who was granted citizenship.
Are we really going to create a second class of U.S. citizens, where we constantly call into question who is and who is not a citizen? By empowering U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to ``review'' all immigration benefits granted to individuals from travel ban countries since January 20, 2021, the Majority is calling into question the settled status of people who have already become citizens--and legal immigrants who have already been heavily vetted. In putting so many lawful immigrants' status at risk simply because of their country of origin, this bill represents a cynical and disgusting attack on legal immigration.
As the Majority mentioned during our Committee markup, their desire to re-vet all these individuals at least partly stems from an alleged fraud scheme that the Administration says largely involves people from the Somali community in Minnesota that has preoccupied right-wing media in recent weeks. Unfortunately, my colleagues seem to leave out an important point: the Biden Administration is the one who initiated this investigation starting in 2022.
Thanks to the previous Administration's work, federal prosecutors have been investigating a series of social services fraud schemes within Minnesota, totaling approximately $1 billion in stolen taxpayer funds which never reached the intended recipients. Over 90 people have been charged and at least 59 people have been convicted to date. For the Majority to pretend that the previous Administration was ignoring fraud or approving people involved in these fraud schemes is just ludicrous.\1\
\1\What To Know About Minnesota's ``Industrial-Scale Fraud'' Scandal, As More Charges Are Filed And Trump Weighs In, CBS News (Dec. 19, 2025), www.cbsnews.com/news/what-to-know-minnesota-fraud-scandal-more-charges-filed-trump-walz/; How Fraud Swamped Minnesota's Social Services System on Tim Walz's Watch, N.Y. Times (Nov. 29, 2025), www.nytimes.com/2025/11/29/us/fraud-minnesota-somali.html; Prosecutors Say Minnesota's Fraud Scandal Goes Further Than Previously Known, N.Y. Times (Dec. 18, 2025), www.nytimes.com/2025/12/18/us/minnesota-fraud-scandal.html.
It is also important to remember, under current law, we already have the ability to denaturalize people in extreme cases, when a judge determines it is appropriate. If an individual has obtained citizenship and the government can show it was obtained illegally, through fraud, or by concealing material facts, they can bring their case forward in court and strip that person of their citizenship if they prove the grounds for revocation.
The same is generally true for lawful permanent residents: if the Department of Homeland Security can show the person was not eligible for the green card to begin with, either because of fraud, misrepresentation, or anything else, they can make their case to an immigration judge. But the idea that we need to authorize a fishing expedition into people whose status has already been determined--based solely on someone's country of origin--is wrong and flies in the face of our Constitution.
This bill is also bizarre because the Trump Administration is currently doing exactly what this bill would authorize. So why are we moving this bill through the House? Does the Majority need to make sure that they too are on the record for opposing legal immigration and second-guessing people's green cards and citizenship years later? Or do they think what the Trump Administration is doing is unlawful and needs an act of Congress?
Regardless, under Republican control, this Committee has steadfastly ignored its oversight duties, instead choosing to serve the whims of an erratic and chaotic President. Democrats, however, refuse to take part in that and will continue to do the serious oversight work this Committee is obligated to perform.
I oppose this legislation, and I urge my colleagues to do the same.
Jamie Raskin,
Ranking Member.
